name: GenAI Security & Compliance Crosswalk Matrix
description: Evidence-grounded crosswalk mapping OWASP GenAI risks to NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, and the EU AI Act.
disclaimer: Independent academic implementation inspired by the mapping concept of the OWASP GenAI Security Project Crosswalk. Conceptual mappings are explicitly indicated.

target_controls.rationale: Directly corresponds to prompt injection technique where untrusted input manipulates model execution context.
Requires evaluating adversarial robustness against prompt injection and evasion techniques.
Requires risk treatment via guardrails to handle untrusted input channels into AI models.
Mandates cybersecurity resilience against unauthorized third parties altering AI behavior via prompt injection.
Directly focuses on privacy and sensitive data protection in prompts, context, and outputs.
Covers unauthorized exfiltration of proprietary or personal data via ML inference queries.
Addresses protection and provenance of sensitive organizational data ingested into AI systems.
Mandates strict data governance and confidentiality safeguards across data used by AI applications.
Addresses ML supply chain compromise through backdoored models, public hubs, or tampered packages.
Requires mapping and managing dependencies on third-party foundation models and components.
Mandates supplier relationship management and risk assessment for third-party AI services.
Requires cybersecurity assurance across AI supply chain dependencies.
Directly maps to adversarial data poisoning of retrieval corpora, databases, or training data.
Addresses data provenance and validation for AI systems to maintain data integrity.
Requires high data quality and prevention of tainted or manipulated data in high-risk AI pipelines.
Specifies verification of AI outputs and fail-safe fallback procedures before executing system actions.
Mandates technical guardrails to treat untrusted model outputs before passing to downstream sinks.
Requires systems to be resilient against secondary injection attacks originating from unsafe model responses.
Directly mandates human oversight and intervention mechanisms for AI actions with significant impact.
Addresses organizational responsibilities, authorization gates, and operational limits on autonomous agents.
Requires identifying risks arising from autonomous tool execution and unconstrained agent permissions.
Corresponds to ML inference extraction of system internals and intellectual property.
Focuses on confidential information disclosure within model system contexts.
Addresses retrieval store integrity, multitenancy partition controls, and vector access controls.
Mandates data governance and access boundaries over vector retrieval corpora.
Addresses operational availability, token rate-limiting, and recursion circuit breakers.
Specifies technical guardrails to prevent denial of service and resource starvation.
